Definition: Abram, the original name of Abraham
BiblicalUsage: Abram is the name Abraham carries for the first part of his story — the son of Terah in Ur, the man called out in Genesis 12:1, ‘Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee.’ He goes out with nothing but the call, and under the stars God promises him a son and a nation before he has either.
TheologicalSignificance: Abram means 'exalted father', and he is an old man with no child when God calls him — the name is almost a joke until God renames him. I believe the Abram years teach me that God calls people before they look like anything: the call comes first, the child comes later, and the land comes last.
